newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 15.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 15.

text.p: Three Gulf of Mexico ports remained shut because of storms in the Gulf of Mexico on Monday, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1500 local/2000 GMT daily meteorological report.

Crude ports Pajaritos and Dos Bocas remained closed for a fourth consecutive day after storms first shut the ports on Saturday afternoon. Winds in the region were reported at up to 60 km per hour and waves up to 13 feet high.
Port officials said the crude terrminals would not be likely to open until Wednesday morning.
Ciudad del Carmen was also reported closed with winds up to 35 km per hour.

Frontera, Nautla, Veracruz, Alvarado and Cayo Arcas were reported closed to smaller fishing and tourism ships. Smaller vessels were also warned against sailing along the coasts of Tamaulipas, Veracruz, Tabasco and the Gulf of Tehuantepec.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.

Stronger winds along northern coastline of 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour) and waves six to nine feet high. Less windy further down coast, except in the Gulf of Tehuantepec, where gusts relaxing from 15 to 20 knots and waves six to nine feet high.

Light rains along the coast of Tamaulipas, Veracruz and Tabasco. Winds at 20 knots and waves six to nine feet high, expect Yucatan peninsula where winds calmer at 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per hour).
Cloudy with some rains and winds from 20 to 30 km per hour.
